title: Should You Trim Or Add To Your Rivian Position Now?

Should You Trim Or Add To Your Rivian Position Now?

Rivian Makes Money On Software And Services

In fiscal Q3 2026, all of Rivian's gross profit came from its Software and Services segment. Management gave these figures on its October 29, 2026 call. The segment generated $605 million in revenue, up 45% from a year earlier. The segment's gross profit was $256 million. About 60% of its revenue came from Rivian's joint venture with Volkswagen Group.

By contrast, Rivian's cars posted an automotive gross loss of $80 million in the quarter, against a $130 million loss a year earlier. Management said about $120 million of the quarter's costs came from building the R2 below a normal production rate. Management also said that automotive gross profit was positive for the quarter when measured on a cash basis and excluding regulatory credits. Under the reported measure, however, the vehicles generated $1.55 billion of revenue while continuing to lose money.

Can Rivian Make Money On Its Cars?

Management expects the cars to reach a gross profit by the end of 2026, though not for a full quarter. During the call, management said the R2 should help Rivian reach a positive automotive gross margin exit rate for the year, adding that it would not expect a full fourth quarter of automotive gross profit.

Volume is part of that plan. The R2 outsold both the R1 and the electric delivery van in the third quarter. Rivian also raised the low end of its 2026 delivery guidance, to 67,000 to 70,000 vehicles from 65,000 to 70,000.

Costs are moving the other way. Management said rising costs of core components have hurt profitability and will keep doing so. It named memory as one cost running well above what Rivian expected. The company is exploring ways to offset those expenses while maintaining a base R2 trim that starts at $45,000, management added.

What Are You Paying For Rivian Stock?

At the November 17, 2026 close, the stock cost 2.7 times Rivian's sales over the past twelve months, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500. A price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful, because Rivian lost money over those twelve months. Its operating margin over the twelve months to September 30, 2026 was -52.9%, against 18.9% for the S&P 500. A sales multiple only modestly below the market's on a business this far from an operating profit suggests buyers are paying for the gross profit that R2 and the software business might earn later.

Waiting for that profit costs Rivian cash. Rivian's free cash flow over those twelve months was negative $4.19 billion, compared with negative $0.489 billion a year earlier. The company held $5.5 billion of cash and short-term investments at September 30, 2026. At the past year's rate of cash use, that would last a little over a year. Management put its total available liquidity and targeted future capital at about $13 billion. That figure counts expected money from Uber, Volkswagen and its Department of Energy loan, all of it subject to conditions.

title: Elon Musk deepfake nearly costs coinbase users $4.7 million
detail:
Elon Musk deepfake nearly costs coinbase users $4.7 million
Bibhu Pattnaik
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:26 PM MST 2 min read
COIN
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Coinbase said Tuesday that its AI-powered scam defenses stopped $4.7 million in customer transfers to fraudsters running a deepfake Elon Musk livestream.

The fake broadcast reached more than 500,000 viewers, Coinbase said in a blog post. Within about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the scammers.

Related: If you invested $1,000 in Trump Media on its first day, here's what it's worth today

A fake Musk and a doubling promise

According to Coinbase, the fraudsters ran a fake YouTube livestream timed to Tesla's flying-car demonstration in October.

The AI-generated Musk told viewers that any crypto sent to listed wallet addresses would come back at twice the value.

No Coinbase accounts were hacked. Customers approved the transfers themselves, which is why passwords and standard account protections could not help. Coinbase said its system pairs machine-learning transaction monitoring with a dedicated scam-prevention AI agent.

The agent flagged the payments, spoke to customers and explained the warning signs of a giveaway scam.

Coinbase said the agent stopped about 91% of the money without human intervention, even though it had not been trained on this type of scam. Coinbase has not said how much reached the scammers or whether any of it was recovered.

Binance hack keeps the pressure on

The incident follows the Oct. 29 Binance breach, in which hackers drained about $6.3 billion in roughly 20 minutes. The FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group, and Pyongyang has denied involvement. Binance said it would cover customer losses with its own funds.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has since warned that hackers are getting AI tools faster than financial institutions can deploy defenses. 

The numbers support the concern. 

The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report put crypto fraud losses at about $11.4 billion, up 22% from 2024. It also logged 22,364 AI-related complaints worth nearly $893 million. 

Coinbase said it plans to invest more in AI-based fraud prevention. Automated checks cannot cover customers who send funds from external wallets or platforms without similar controls.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares are down 15.48% year to date at $380.11 and up just 4.01% over five years. Under the hood, the business is moving quickly. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million, up from 1.04 million a year ago.

Even so, consensus calls for 2027 EPS of $2.1592, 25% above the 2026 estimate of $1.7242. Revenue is expected to reach $122.4 billion, which would represent 13.5% growth. Tesla has beaten EPS estimates in three of the last four quarters. In Q3 it reported $0.48 against a $0.4511 estimate.

TSLA Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.
Here's What It Takes for Tesla to Reach $600

Tesla currently trades at 176x 2027 estimated earnings. At $600, the multiple would rise to 278x. The 2027 estimates are spread widely, though. Measured against the most bullish 2027 EPS forecast of $4.13, $600 works out to 145x, cheaper than today's multiple on consensus.

So the path to $600 depends on estimates moving toward the high end. Revisions have recently gone the other way: the consensus figure is down from $2.2520 90 days ago.

TSLA Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St.
What Could Push Tesla to $600?

Robotaxi revenue: Musk said Robotaxi revenue should become noticeable around Q2 and "a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year." Unsupervised miles grew 8x in the quarter to nearly 2 million.

FSD monetization: More than 75% of North American Q3 deliveries came with a paid FSD sign-up. On the call, Vaibhav Taneja confirmed an analyst's estimate of about $1 billion in FSD annual recurring revenue.

Energy: Musk said Tesla is almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027. Energy gross margin rose to 33.1% from 20.4%, helped in part by tariff refunds.

Optimus: Management expects to start shipping robots to outside customers toward the end of next year, with the AI5 chip integrated around April.

SpaceX merger: Barclays upgraded Tesla to Overweight on October 26 and raised its target to $450 from $370. The firm pointed to upside from the expected merger with SpaceX and to data center demand.

Tesla's History Says $600 Is Possible

A $600 share price would need a 57.8% gain. Tesla has hit that level four times since 2011, using split-adjusted year-end prices. Shares rose 743% in 2020, 344% in 2013, 102% in 2023 and 62.5% in 2024. Big moves cut both ways: the stock fell 65% in 2022.

With a market cap near $1.50 trillion, another 2020 is unlikely. The 2023 and 2024 gains, however, show how fast this stock can be appreciated once sentiment changes.

Why $600 Is a Stretch Worth Studying

Getting to $600 would take a 57.8% gain in 2027, well above Wall Street's $412.48 target.

The bull case rests on three things: Robotaxi turning into real revenue, FSD subscriptions continuing to compound and Megapack demand holding up. The main hurdles are rising operating expenses, capex guidance of about $20 billion for this year and falling EPS revisions.

Waymo Ordered Off California Freeways for an "Imminent Hazard to Public Safety." Tesla Has More at Stake ©U.S. Air Force photo and Bl∡ke from Pexels via Canva]
Key Takeaways

California's DMV ordered Alphabet's Waymo off the state's freeways, calling its driverless freeway operations "an imminent hazard to public safety."

Tesla has far more at stake: it trades at about 178x forward earnings, compared with about 20x for Alphabet.

Tesla needs the same regulators' approval, and in California it holds only a permit to test with a driver.

Uber runs robotaxis from many companies, so one maker's setback hurts it less. Tesla's next test is its fourth-quarter report in late January.

California just ordered Waymo, the robotaxi unit of Alphabet (GOOG), off the state's freeways.

The DMV said on Tuesday that the ban took effect last week, after a series of incidents in which Waymo robotaxis drove into active construction zones. "The Department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety," it said.

Waymo then paused freeway rides in its other US markets too, though its cars still run on city streets.

All-In podcast co-host Jason Calacanis summed up the risk in a post on X:

"If Autonomy makes but one mistake, they risk an entire state."

That's a much bigger problem for Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) than for Alphabet. And Uber Technologies (UBER:NYSE) has its own stake in how regulators react.

Tesla's price is a bet on autonomy

Elon Musk posted on X on Oct. 17 that "Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla's value."

Analysts expect revenue to climb from $94.8 billion in 2025 to $146 billion in 2028, after it slipped from $96.8 billion in 2023:

Tesla (TSLA): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

That's healthy growth, but profits lag well behind it. Consensus has normalized EPS at $3.30 in 2028, still below the $4.07 Tesla earned in 2022.

Even so, Tesla trades at 178x forward earnings, above its three-year average of 138x:

Tesla (TSLA): forward (NTM) P/E, last 3 years (TIKR)

At that price, investors are paying for robotaxi and robot profits that the 2028 estimates don't show yet. So every regulator's decision on robotaxis bears directly on Tesla's stock.

TIKR tracks 44 analysts on Tesla. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla's Analyst Ratings

Alphabet can shrug this off

Alphabet trades at 20x forward earnings, below its three-year average of 23x:

Alphabet (GOOG): forward (NTM) P/E, last 3 years (TIKR)

At 20x, investors are paying for what search, cloud and YouTube earn today. For Alphabet, this is a setback for one unit that investors weren't paying much for in the first place.
